4.3.4.4 Accessing NvM in multicore/multipartition configurations
A system using multiple cores or EcucPartitions may map NVBlocks to a specific EcucPartition. Based on these mappings, an RTE shall implement protection (such as the use of IOC or CallTrustedFunction) to cross partition protection boundaries in certain circumstances. NVBlocks are mapped to a specific partition through the use of the ECUC parameter NvMBlockEcucPartitionRef [ECUC_NvM_00564] which is set on an NvMBlockDescriptor.
[SWS_Rte_03897] Upstream requirements: SRS_Rte_00176, SRS_Rte_00177
⌈The RTE Generator shall reject configurations where the EcucPartition which references an NvBlockSwComponentType (via ECUC parameter EcucPartitionSoftwareComponentInstanceRef) does not match the EcucPartition referenced by all NvMBlockDescriptors (via the ECUC parameter NvMBlockEcucPartitionRef) associated with that NvBlockSwComponentType.⌋ Note: NvMBlockDescriptors associated with an NvBlockSwComponentType can be found via the ECUC container RteNvRamAllocation. Specifically, NvBlockDescriptors are aggregated by an NvBlockSwComponentType, which are then mapped to a corresponding NvMBlockDescriptor (from the NvM) by an RteNvRamAllocation via the ECUC parameters RteSwNvBlockDescriptorRef and RteNvmBlockRef.
[SWS_Rte_03898] Upstream requirements: SRS_Rte_00176, SRS_Rte_00177
⌈The RTE Generator shall support configurations where a VariableDataPrototype instance in the role NvBlockDescriptor.ramBlock of a NvBlockSwComponentType is accessed by SW-C instances of different partitions.⌋ Note: Support for these communication scenarios follows the usual rules for port based communication which crosses EcucPartition boundaries and must obey the requirements in section 4.3.4. The RTE must offer a number of callbacks to the NvM module for updating/reading RTE data mirrors or notifying the RTE of the status of NvM jobs. A system using multiple cores or EcucPartitions may map NVBlocks to a specific EcucPartition. Based on these mappings, an RTE shall implement protection (such as the use of IOC or CallTrustedFunction) to cross partition protection boundaries in certain circumstances.
